units.title: Domain A: Digital Awareness and Wellbeing

outcomes.text: Trace how technology has changed.
Discover that technology brings both opportunities and challenges.
Reflect on how wisely society adapts to new technologies.
Learn how people have communicated, from smoke signals to smartphones.
Discover what 'media' means.
Uncover the real story behind media as a media detective.
Question everything to understand the world of media better.

units.title: Domain C: Digital Civility and Ethics

outcomes.text: Understand community membership and how citizenship powers can be used online and offline.
Learn the principles of digital citizenship with 'superhero' powers for safe, kind online spaces.
Explore how online actions shape digital identity and reputation.
Learn how personal information is stored in the cloud and how to protect privacy.
Understand why ethical, respectful choices online matter and how online behaviour affects people.
Share information thoughtfully, using privacy settings to manage visibility.
Communicate politely and constructively in digital spaces.
Manage and protect your online reputation with empathy, kindness and critical thinking.

units.title: Domain D: Safety, Privacy and Wellbeing

outcomes.text: Apply essential online safety rules and responsible behaviour.
Identify malware, the risks of untrusted downloads and the role of security software and updates.
Recognise online scams, scammer tactics and how to respond.
Understand digital identity: profiles, bios and selfies, and express yourself truthfully.
Value empathy and diversity, tell hate speech from unkind words and respond to it.
Explore identity safely and tell genuine from misleading online behaviour.
Question everything to understand the world of media better.

units.title: Domain A: Digital Awareness and Wellbeing

outcomes.text: Understand what digital stress is and how it affects us.
Spot digital distractions and what they do to our lives.
Handle persuasive technologies and avoid their tricks.
See why balancing screen time with green time matters.
Understand social media addiction and its effects on the brain.
Identify feelings of FOMO, low self-esteem, comparison and envy from social media.
Develop strategies for a healthier relationship with social media.

units.title: Domain A: Digital Awareness and Wellbeing

outcomes.text: Grasp accessibility and inclusivity in digital media.
Explore how assistive technology helps people with disabilities use digital media.
Understand how inclusive media shapes society.
Identify obstacles to accessibility in digital media.
Get to know the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).
Make strategies for more accessible and inclusive media.
Apply WCAG to evaluate a website.

units.title: Domain E: Research and Content Use

outcomes.text: Choose keywords and build queries, using advanced tools for better academic searches.
Evaluate search results for academic reliability and credible sources.
Cite sources, build a bibliography and use different citation styles.
Spot and avoid plagiarism by referencing properly and using sources ethically.
Identify what lets social media bring change, and its harms.
Practise responsible online activism and respectful participation.
Understand digital citizenship and the results of online actions.
Grasp what AI is, how it works, large language models, and AI's benefits, limits and challenges.
Use information literacy to assess AI-generated content, bias, privacy and security.
Explore what deepfakes are, how they are made, benefits, harms and ethical and legal challenges.
Learn ways to detect and prevent deepfakes and engage responsibly with AI content.

units.title: Domain B: Media and Information Literacy

outcomes.text: Understand the purpose and types of advertising and the techniques used to sway buyers.
Analyse how advertising shapes consumer behaviour, perceptions and choices.
Navigate online advertising by understanding how user data is collected and used for targeting.
Analyse news content, telling real news from opinion, satire, misinformation, disinformation, malinformation and fake news.
Use lateral reading, source checks and clickbait awareness to judge news credibility.
Trace the history of photo manipulation and build visual literacy for reading images.
Understand the psychological effect of photo manipulation and tell enhanced visuals from the real product.

units.title: Domain C: Digital Civility and Ethics

outcomes.text: Tell cyberbullying from digital drama and recognise their emotional and psychological impact.
Define online disinhibition and how it feeds cyberbullying and hidden identities.
Build empathy and ethical behaviour online and refuse to join or tolerate bullying.
Use a three-step strategy to handle and prevent cyberbullying.
Recognise roles in bullying and move from bystander to active supporter.

units.title: Domain D: Safety, Privacy and Wellbeing

outcomes.text: Understand personal information and how online services use it.
Learn what doxing is, its methods, and how to protect personal information.
Use strong passwords and Two-Factor Authentication for lifelong digital safety.
Understand privacy policies and Terms of Use and assess digital agreements critically.
Understand algorithms and the filter bubble and how to protect privacy.
Debate the ethical, social and technical sides of digital privacy dilemmas.

units.title: Domain E: Research and Content Use

outcomes.text: Understand intellectual property and copyright law.
Respect others' creative work online and see how Creative Commons licences protect and share it.
Grasp Creative Commons licence types and how to apply them to your own work.
Understand the Public Domain and find examples of works in it.
Learn about Fair Use and use copyrighted material respectfully under it.
Weigh the ethical and legal sides of IP, Creative Commons, Public Domain and Fair Use.
Understand bias and cognitive bias and how social media interacts with human psychology.
Analyse stereotypes and biases in media and the effect on people and society.
Analyse media messages for stereotypes, bias and hidden assumptions.
Challenge stereotypes and create alternative messages that show diverse views.
Evaluate truths and myths about sexism and recognise online sexism.
